K-Shell Based Gravity Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch65.R
centrality_ksgc.Rd

K-shell based gravity centrality (KSGC; Yang and Xiao 2021) is a gravity model in which the pull of a node on another depends on their k-shell indices: $$KSGC(i) = \sum_{j:\,d_{ij} \le \langle d \rangle / 2} \exp\!\Bigl(\frac{ks_i - ks_j}{ks_{max} - ks_{min}}\Bigr) \frac{k_i k_j}{d_{ij}^2},$$ with \(k\) the degree, \(ks\) the k-shell index, \(d_{ij}\) the distance and \(\langle d \rangle\) the average shortest-path length of the network.

Usage

centrality_ksgc(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The radius is half the average path length, used as it is in the test \(d_{ij} \le \langle d \rangle / 2\); it is not rounded, unlike the "auto" radius of centrality_gravity. On a network whose average path length is below 2 no node lies within the radius, and every score is 0. This is the rule of the source, and it makes the measure uninformative on small dense networks. When all nodes are in one shell the exponent is 0/0 and the coefficient is taken as 1, which is the plain gravity model; the source says the method reduces to it when two nodes share a shell. The source covers connected networks; on a disconnected one the average is taken over the pairs that reach each other. Isolated nodes score 0. The source prints no value on a small network, so the implementation is checked against the definition only. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Yang, X. and Xiao, F. (2021). An improved gravity model to identify influential nodes in complex networks based on k-shell method. Knowledge-Based Systems, 227, 107198. doi:10.1016/j.knosys.2021.107198 .

See also

centrality_gravity, centrality_coreness, centrality.

Examples

centrality_ksgc(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>          0          0          0          0          0          0          0 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>          0          0          0
